message.content:
You are black-box reverse-engineering a compiled C++ binary. You MUST NOT look for or read any C++ library source (there is none on disk; `idna.hpp` does not exist). Derive behavior ONLY by running the binary.

BINARY: /workspace/dataset/test4_executable
Invoke as: /workspace/dataset/test4_executable "<domain-string>"
It prints exactly 4 lines, each "1" or "0", in this order:
  line1 = idna::is_valid_domain(input)
  line2 = idna::is_valid_label(input)
  line3 = idna::is_ascii_domain(input)
  line4 = idna::is_idn_domain(input)
With no argument, input defaults to the literal string "example.com".

ENVIRONMENT NOTES (important):
- python3 / python are NOT installed. perl may not be installed.
- Use bash loops, printf, tr, head, sed, awk to build test strings.
- Handy helper you can paste:
    rep() { local n=$1 c=$2 s=""; for ((i=0;i<n;i++)); do s+="$c"; done; printf '%s' "$s"; }
  or:  s=$(head -c 64 /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'a')
- To emit arbitrary/high bytes use: printf '\xNN'  (bash $'...' quoting also works)
- rustc and cargo ARE available if you need a quick generator program.

ALREADY-ESTABLISHED FACTS (verify, do not blindly trust):
- "" (empty)        -> 0 0 1 0
- "example.com"     -> 1 1 1 0
- "例子.测试"        -> 1 1 0 1
- "a"x63            -> 1 1 1 0
- "a"x64            -> 1 0 1 0   (is_valid_label flips off above 63)
- "a"x255           -> 1 0 1 0
- "a"x256           -> 0 0 1 0   (is_valid_domain flips off above 255)
- "." ".." "a." ".a" "a..b" "-a.com" "a-.com" "a_b.com" "a b.com" "a/b.com" "*.com" -> all 1 1 1 0

Be rigorous and quantitative. Bisect every boundary you claim (test N-1, N, N+1). Report exact reproducible command lines as evidence.


YOUR DIMENSION: is_valid_label (line 2).
Note the whole input string is passed as ONE label (the program does not split on dots before calling it).
Determine precisely:
- Exact min/max length. Bisect 0/1 and 62/63/64/65.
- BYTES or CODE POINTS? Build labels of multi-byte UTF-8 chars: 21 copies of "例" = 63 bytes = 21 codepoints; 22 copies = 66 bytes. Test 20/21/22 copies. Also test with 2-byte chars ("ü": 31/32 copies = 62/64 bytes) and 4-byte chars. Pin down whether the limit is 63 bytes or 63 codepoints.
- Does content matter AT ALL? "example.com" (contains dots) returns 1, so dots are allowed. Sweep every ASCII byte 0x01..0x7F alone and embedded. Test hyphens at start/end, all-hyphens, "xn--" prefixes, digits-only, spaces, control chars.
- Is it exactly `len >= 1 && len <= 63`? Try hard to find ANY input of length 1..63 that returns 0, and ANY input of length 0 or >=64 that returns 1. Report the result of that search honestly.

for len in 0 1 2 3 5 8 13 21 34 55 60 61 62 63 64 65 66 70 80 127 128 200 255 256 300; do

rules.statement: is_valid_label(s) is EXACTLY `1 <= byte_length(s) <= 63`. Content is completely irrelevant — it is a pure length check on the raw byte count. No counterexample was found in ~2000 targeted + fuzz + exhaustive tests.
rules.evidence:
Dense sweep, 11 content patterns x lengths 0..70 (781 execs), asserting r == (1<=n<=63):
$ mk() { local n=$1 pat=$2 s=""; while [ ${#s} -lt $n ]; do s+="$pat"; done; printf '%s' "${s:0:$n}"; }
$ for pat in 'a' '-' '.' '_' ' ' 'xn--' 'A1-' '..-' '/\' '*?' $'\t'; do for n in $(seq 0 70); do s=$(mk $n "$pat"); [ $n -eq 0 ] && s=""; r=$(/workspace/dataset/test4_executable "$s"|sed -n 2p); exp=0; [ $n -ge 1 ] && [ $n -le 63 ] && exp=1; [ "$r" = "$exp" ] || echo "FAIL pat=[$pat] n=$n got=$r exp=$exp"; done; done
-> dense ASCII length sweep 0..70 x 11 patterns: counterexamples=0

rules.statement: Minimum length is 1: the empty string is the ONLY input that returns 0 on the low side. Any 1-byte input returns 1.
rules.evidence:
$ /workspace/dataset/test4_executable ""  | tr '\n' ' '   ->  0 0 1 0    (line2 = 0)
$ /workspace/dataset/test4_executable "a" | tr '\n' ' '   ->  1 1 1 0    (line2 = 1)
Exhaustive: every single byte value 0x01..0xFF as a 1-byte label returns 1 (see per-byte rule below). Since argv cannot carry a NUL, "" is the only length-0 input reachable, and it returns 0.

rules.statement: Maximum length is 63 (inclusive). Bisected: 62 -> 1, 63 -> 1, 64 -> 0, 65 -> 0. The flip is between 63 and 64.
rules.evidence:
$ for n in 62 63 64 65; do printf "%d: %s\n" $n "$(/workspace/dataset/test4_executable "$(head -c $n /dev/zero|tr '\0' a)"|tr '\n' ' ')"; done
62: 1 1 1 0
63: 1 1 1 0
64: 1 0 1 0
65: 1 0 1 0
Also 66,100,1000,10000,100000 -> line2 = 0.

rules.statement: The limit is counted in BYTES, not code points, and not UTF-8 characters. Decisive: 16 x U+1F600 is 16 code points but 64 bytes and returns 0; 15 x U+1F600 + "aaa" is 18 code points but 63 bytes and returns 1.
rules.evidence:
$ /workspace/dataset/test4_executable "😀😀😀😀😀😀😀😀😀😀😀😀😀😀😀aaa" | tr '\n' ' '
1 1 0 1     <- 63 bytes, 18 codepoints -> line2=1
$ /workspace/dataset/test4_executable "😀😀😀😀😀😀😀😀😀😀😀😀😀😀😀😀" | tr '\n' ' '
1 0 0 1     <- 64 bytes, 16 codepoints -> line2=0
If the limit were code points, 16 cp <= 63 would pass and 18 cp would also pass; the observed split tracks bytes exactly.

rules.statement: Byte-counting is confirmed independently for 2-byte, 3-byte and 4-byte UTF-8 sequences: the pass/fail flip always lands at 63/64 BYTES regardless of character width.
rules.evidence:
3-byte 例 (E4 BE 8B):  x20=60B ->1 1 0 1 ; x21=63B ->1 1 0 1 ; x22=66B ->1 0 0 1  (22 cp would pass if cp-based)
2-byte ü (C3 BC):     x31=62B ->1 1 0 1 ; x32=64B ->1 0 0 1
Mixed to hit exact 63: "ü"x31 + "a"x1 = 63B -> 1 1 0 1 ; "ü"x31 + "a"x2 = 64B -> 1 0 0 1
4-byte 😀: x15+a x3 = 63B -> 1 1 0 1 ; x15+a x4 = 64B -> 1 0 0 1 ; x14=56B ->1 1 0 1 ; x16=64B ->1 0 0 1
Commands used: rep(){ local n=$1 c=$2 s=""; for ((i=0;i<n;i++)); do s+="$c"; done; printf '%s' "$s"; }; /workspace/dataset/test4_executable "$(rep 21 '例')"

rules.statement: Content matters ZERO. Every byte value 0x01..0xFF is accepted, both as a solo 1-byte label and embedded mid-label. There is no character-class filter, no UTF-8 validity check, no ASCII restriction.

rules.statement: Exhaustive per-byte-value boundary check: for ALL 255 reachable byte values, a homogeneous string of length 1 -> 1, length 63 -> 1, length 64 -> 0. The boundary is content-independent.
rules.evidence:
$ for i in $(seq 1 255); do h=$(printf '%02x' $i); f63=""; for ((j=0;j<63;j++)); do f63+="\\x$h"; done; printf -v s63 "$f63"; printf -v s64 "$f63\\x$h"; printf -v s1 "\\x$h"; r1=$(/workspace/dataset/test4_executable "$s1"|sed -n 2p); r63=$(/workspace/dataset/test4_executable "$s63"|sed -n 2p); r64=$(/workspace/dataset/test4_executable "$s64"|sed -n 2p); [ "$r1$r63$r64" = "110" ] || echo "0x$h=$r1$r63$r64"; done
-> per-byte (len1,len63,len64) expect 110 -> anomalies:NONE
(printf -v is used instead of $(...) so trailing 0x0a bytes are preserved.)

rules.statement: No IDNA/LDH/hostname semantics are applied: leading/trailing/all hyphens, underscores, dots, spaces, slashes, wildcards, colons, digits-only, uppercase, and both well-formed and malformed "xn--" prefixes all return 1 when 1..63 bytes.
rules.evidence:
105-input content battery, all asserted against `1<=len<=63`, 0 counterexamples. Representative singles:

$ /workspace/dataset/test4_executable "---------"    -> 1 1 1 0

Battery included: hyphen/underscore/dot placements, xn-- variants and case, IPv4/IPv6 literals, URL forms, punctuation, ZWJ/ZWNJ (U+200C/U+200D), ideographic full stop U+3002, fullwidth forms, Arabic-Indic digits, ß, İ, ﬀ, ℀, café/CAFÉ.

rules.statement: Randomized byte-level fuzzing found no deviation: 200 random binary strings across 25 lengths (0..300) all matched `1 <= bytes <= 63`.
rules.evidence:
$ RANDOM=12345; for len in 0 1 2 3 5 8 13 21 34 55 60 61 62 63 64 65 66 70 80 127 128 200 255 256 300; do for trial in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; do fmt=""; for ((i=0;i<len;i++)); do fmt+=$(printf '\\x%02x' $(( (RANDOM % 255) + 1 ))); done; printf -v s "$fmt"; r=$(/workspace/dataset/test4_executable "$s"|sed -n 2p); exp=0; [ $len -ge 1 ] && [ $len -le 63 ] && exp=1; [ "$r" != "$exp" ] && echo MISMATCH; done; done
-> fuzz total=200 mismatches=0

rules.statement: Directed search for counterexamples FAILED in both directions: no input of length 1..63 was found that returns 0, and no input of length 0 or >=64 was found that returns 1. Total ~2000 executions across exhaustive per-byte, dense pattern sweep, content battery, and random fuzz.
rules.evidence:
Aggregate of the four campaigns above:
- 255x2 byte sweep (solo + embedded): 0 real anomalies
- 255x3 exhaustive per-byte at len 1/63/64: anomalies NONE
- 781 dense pattern x length sweep (0..70): counterexamples=0
- 105 hand-crafted adversarial content battery: counterexamples=0
- 200 random binary fuzz (len 0..300): mismatches=0
Honest result: the hypothesis `len>=1 && len<=63` survived every attack.

rules.statement: Behavior is deterministic and the binary never crashes or changes exit status; huge inputs (100 KB ASCII, 90 KB multibyte) return line2=0 with exit code 0.
rules.evidence:
$ for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do /workspace/dataset/test4_executable "$(head -c 63 /dev/urandom | tr -dc 'a-zA-Z0-9')" | sed -n 2p; done  -> 1 1 1 1 1
$ /workspace/dataset/test4_executable "$(head -c 100000 /dev/zero|tr '\0' a)" | tr '\n' ' '  -> 0 0 1 0
$ s=$(head -c 30000 /dev/zero|tr '\0' x); s=${s//x/例}; /workspace/dataset/test4_executable "$s" | tr '\n' ' '  -> 0 0 0 1   (90000 bytes)
$ /workspace/dataset/test4_executable "abc" >/dev/null; echo rc=$?   -> rc=0
$ /workspace/dataset/test4_executable ""    >/dev/null; echo rc=$?   -> rc=0

rules.statement: With no argument the program uses the default "example.com", producing line2=1 — identical to explicitly passing "example.com".

openQuestions: Embedded NUL (0x00) behavior is untestable through argv, so it is unknown whether the length is measured on a NUL-terminated C string or on a length-carrying std::string/string_view. Any Rust reimplementation taking &str/&[u8] should assume byte length of the full slice; this is unobservable from this harness.

The implementation is indistinguishable from `s.size() >= 1 && s.size() <= 63` (equivalently `!s.empty() && s.size() <= 63`, or `(1..=63).contains(&s.len())`). Whether the upper bound is a literal 63 or a named constant derived from 64-1 cannot be determined black-box.

Line 2 shows no interaction with lines 1/3/4: is_valid_label is independent of is_valid_domain (255-byte cap), is_ascii_domain, and is_idn_domain. Confirmed for all tested inputs but not formally proven for every combination.
Behavior for inputs longer than the OS ARG_MAX (~2 MB) was not probed; execution fails at the shell level before reaching the binary, so the 63-byte rule is only verified up to 100 KB.
